title.narrative: Sustainable Coastal and Marine Fisheries Project

description.narrative:
The project invests in increasing the climate resilience and sustainability of coastal and marine fisheries in Cambodia, targeting the four coastal provinces of Cambodia - Kampot, Kep, Koh Kong, and Preah Sihanouk to reverse the sharp decline in fisheries, promote sustainable mariculture, and enhance fish landing sites to improve seafood safety. It is expected that about 40% of the nearshore fishery will be regenerated into a more productive and sustainable fishery. It will make significant contributions to enhance adaptation to climate change. The project will also promote private sector development by enabling coastal communities and small businesses to diversify their livelihoods, adopt sustainable practices, and scale up into viable enterprises. It will support women's economic empowerment by scaling up women's engagement in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The project will benefit 25 community fisheries (CFi) organizations and members of 15 community protected areas (CPAs), comprising nearly 20,000 households, and a wider coastal community of about 200,000.
The project is aligned with the following impact: coastal and marine fisheries resources made sustainable and resilient. The project will have the following outcome: coastal and marine fish stocks recovered, and diversified climate-resilient income generated. To achieve this outcome, the project has 3 key outputs. Output 1 will support enhancement of adaptive coastal and marine fisheries, which targets changes in the use and management of priority ecosystems and fisheries to reduce the likelihood of their continued decline and build their resilience to underlying climate change threats. Output 2 will support investments in climate-resilient and gender inclusive coastal infrastructure for fisheries management including nature-based infrastructure solutions for coastal erosion, climate risk reduction, and fishery productivity. Output 3 will support incubation and commercialization of sustainable and inclusive marine businesses.

Fish biomass increased by 30% (2022 baseline: TBD) Progress/Status: There are two types of devices involved: 5,000 Fish Protection Structures (FPS) provided by MCC, and 2,500 Fish Boxes supported by the Department of Fisheries Conservation. Fish Protection Structures (FPS):
• A total deployment of 5,000 FPS under MCC. As of Q2 2026, 1500 structures have been deployed, with the next priority locations identified in northern Kampot and Sre Ambel. For Sre Ambel specifically, the use of a second-hand barge has been identified as a cost-effective and practical method for deployment, considering the local conditions.
The deployment activities have significantly contributed to the protection and restoration of marine habitats, deterrence to destructive fishing practices in the critical habitat area and promoting the return of marine mammals such as dolphins and dugongs, as well as the regrowth of seagrass ecosystems. These ecological improvements are fostering opportunities for agritourism (nature-based tourism), which in turn supports sustainable and reliable livelihoods for local communities. In addition, the project emphasizes community participation and capacity building, ensuring that local people are actively involved including women and youth, and empowered in both the deployment and conservation efforts with skills.
• Fish Boxes: The Department of Fisheries Conservation is overseeing the deployment of 2,500 fish boxes, and has carried out technical consultations and on-site assessments. As of Q2 2026, through series of public consultations 38 locations within CFis in Kep, Kampot, and Preah Sihanouk province were identified and digitally demarcated as potential area for the block deployment, and are scheduled to finish in Koh Kong province in Q1 2026. In parallel, the two redesigned fish boxes is ready in Q4 2025 for the testing construction and deployment with communities in Kep, and Kampot in Q1 2026. The Department has also compiled X/Y spatial data of previously installed fish boxes supported by other projects, and is reviewing alternative reef structures—particularly from the Stichting ReefSystems Foundation—for compatibility with local marine substrate data. Data Source: Annual monitoring reports for areas where fish productivity structures are deployed. Actual value:

Output: Adaptive coastal and marine fisheries enhanced Indicator: Additional 7800 fishery productivity structures deployed Achievement: 1500 Progress/Status: The Marine Conservation Cambodia (MCC) Organization to help with the deployment of the fishery productivity structures mobilized on 1 Jan 2024. Since its mobilization, it has deployed a total of 1,500 FPS in Kampot and Sre Ambel .
Contract for the FiA-GD28 to supply Fisheries Slabs awarded in Oct 2024.
After more than one year of negotiation, procurement for the 2nd hand barge was declared unsuccessful in Q1 2026. Technical specification has been updated. A much more nearer supplier has been identified. Contract award is expected by end of Q3 2026 and deployed by Q4 2026.
Deployment of fish boxes. Through consultations, 43 fish box sites were identified across four provinces for deployment in 3-4 meter water depth: 7 in Kep, 15 in Kampot, 12 in Preah Sihanouk, and 9 in Koh Kong. In collaboration with CFis, the structure has been redesigned and tested with new bolts, and alternative construction materials are being explored to reduce weight, as the current concrete boxes are too heavy for efficient shallow-water deployment. The testing also confirmed that a single design is not suitable for all shallow-water conditions, and that different structures will be needed to provide effective juvenile habitats across varying seabed substrates. The new low draft barge was bided but failed. An early market engagement was conducted this July 2026. Successful procurement is expected by Q4 2026. .

Output: Adaptive coastal and marine fisheries enhanced Indicator: Water quality monitoring, algal bloom monitoring, and biotoxicity early warning systems established and made operational (2022 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: 20 CFis received basic trainings on Water Quality, and 10 communities selected as pilot sites for the water quality and biotoxin monitoring for the first phase after series of technical training to the community level on basic water qualities suitable to nearshore non-fed mariculture. Building on the progress of previous quarters, MARDEC, MAFREDI and CS-01 have applied basic monitoring water quality and nutrient for non-feed mariculture through testing/demonstration of non-feed mariculture in seven communities (one in Kep, one in Kampot, one in Preah Sihanouk, and four in Koh Kong). This activity will complement Sub-output 1.5 and 1.6. Preliminary observations from the demonstration sites in two CFis in Koh Kong suggest that the water quality remains favorable for non-fed mariculture. Both oyster and green mussel spat showed attachment rates exceeding 50%, indicating promising site suitability for spat collection and grow-out. However, barnacle attachment was also recorded at approximately 80%, which presents a significant biofouling challenge for non-fed farming and may reduce production efficiency through competition for space and resources. Other sites will be reported in Q2 2026. The demonstration will inform the project on potential scalability and responds to the road map for non-fed mariculture. Data Source: FiA quarterly and annual progress reports; survey reports and data sets from surveys in the FIMS; climate relevant parameters (temperature, precipitation, sea level rise, and extreme event) and data from MOWRAM, as a hydromet agency; and biotoxicity monitoring data in FIMS Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Climate-resilient coastal infrastructure developed Indicator: Climate-resilient infrastructure built: (i) one government office to house the vessel monitoring system and two Fisheries Administration Cantonment offices; (ii) two vessels' jetties replaced; (iii) at least eight landing sites modernized, including gender-responsive and child-safe design; (iv) at least four community infrastructures for fisheries built; and (v) at least six community-protected area tourism infrastructures constructed—all with gender-responsive and inclusive design features (2022 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: The Kep Office is completed and inagurated on 9 Jul 2026.
The VMS building in Sihanoukville has reached approximately 90% completion, while construction of the Kampot FiAC has commenced.
Construction of Preah Sihanouk FiA Marine Inspectorate Boat Mooring and Jetty (SCMFP FiA/CW-03/2026-01) awarded on 19 Jan 2026.
The detailed engineering designs (DEDs) for two landing sites in Sre Ambel, Koh Kong, have been finalized and are progressing toward civil works procurement. The jetty for the FiA Inspectorate in Sihanoukville is under procurement, and the Kampot boat jetty location has been approved and is moving into the design stage
Progress is also being made on fisheries landing sites. Two sites in Koh Kong are in the bidding process, two sites in Kep are undergoing design revisions, three sites in Sihanoukville are at the concept design stage, and one site in Kampot is under architectural design. The project aims to advance at least four landing sites to construction within this year. Twenty-two community fisheries infrastructure sites in 4 provinces were screened (5 in Koh Kong, 4 in Kep, 8 in Sihanoukville and 5 in Kampot), of which 13 sites have passed. Four of these have completed screening and entered the concept design stage, with further site prioritization being undertaken in coordination with DACP to ensure complementarity with other development partners. The redesign of several facilities is ongoing to accommodate updated requirements and stakeholder feedback. In Kep, the landing site has been moved and design modifications are underway which needs to (i) extend its pier possibly by 500 meters to access sufficient depth across all tides, (ii) confirm the number and size of vessels that will use the revised site and then reflect this within the revised design as small trawlers are not expected to move to the new site; and (iii) to be gender-responsive and include space for childcare facilities. The change will require a revised social impact consultation, and confirmation of land ownership. The Phsar Kdam landing site at the Kep Crab Market is one of Kep's priority sites, is being redesigned at the request of the provincial governor to align with the new tourism development plans, including the upgraded crab market area.

Output: Climate-resilient coastal infrastructure developed Indicator: Nature-based infrastructure established through (i) 30,000 ha of mangrove mapped, demarcated, and titled; (ii) 510 ha protected from sea level rise; (iii) 130 ha of Rhizophora planted; and (iv) 1,100 ha of mangrove rehabilitated (2022 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Selected mangrove restoration sites have been identified in seven CPAs, with no apparent land-use conflicts. However, nursery readiness needs to be reviewed, including seedling availability and species composition. The review will be completed by end of June. Planning is required across the full cycle, including nursery preparation, planting, capacity building and needs assessment, cost estimation, and community preparation under the CPP approach. Timely seed collection (within one month) is critical, as delays could affect planting this year. CS-01 is requested to prioritize mangrove restoration activities under MOE to achieve climate adaptation goals. Further details on mangrove planning are indicated in section A. Some progress has been made for the construction of ranger stations under MOE, however still at screening and stakeholder consultation. SCMFP MOE/CS-01 is preparing DDR for these stations. Data Source: Project progress reports; mangrove monitoring report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y
